data.narrative:
World Labs, a Series A AI & Software company founded by Fei-Fei Li, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner, and Justin Johnson, has raised $1.23B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on two primary methodologies applied against a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables spanning both Series A and Series B rounds.

Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $1.2B total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next funding stage, implies a valuation of $2.5B. Peer-median methodology proves more instructive: the four-company comparable set (Reflection AI at $25.0B, Together AI at $8.3B, Physical Intelligence at $5.6B, and Black Forest Labs at $3.2B) yields a median valuation of $7.0B, with a range spanning $3.2B to $25.0B. The wide dispersion reflects substantial variation in perceived stage advancement and market sentiment within frontier AI infrastructure.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $8.0B (high), with a median of $4.7B. The disparity between stage-progression and peer-median estimates reflects tension between capital-deployed methodology and market comparables. Key uncertainties include whether World Labs commands a premium to its peer cohort given founder pedigree, and the degree to which recent AI infrastructure funding momentum has inflated public market multiples relative to private-round fundamentals.
